title: Batch file CLI with a plan, dry run and undo log
when: A CLI renames, moves or rewrites many files at once and the user wants to preview every change, catch conflicts before touching disk, and undo a run.
prompt:
Goal: Plan every operation first, check conflicts, show the plan, then apply with atomic writes and an undo journal.
Steps:
1. Plan phase: scan inputs into an array of { op: "rename" | "write" | "delete", from, to } without touching disk.
2. Check the plan: two sources to one target, an existing target outside the plan, cycles (a to b, b to a), paths leaving the root after path.resolve; list all conflicts, exit 2.
3. --dry-run is the default: print "rename  old.txt -> new.txt" per operation plus totals; --json prints the plan; exit 0.
4. --apply runs operations in plan order; cycles go through temporary names (name.tmp-<random>).
5. Writes go to a temp file in the same folder, then fs.rename over the target, so a crash never leaves half a file.
6. Before each operation append its reverse to .batch-undo.jsonl; batch undo replays it backwards, then removes it.
7. Stop at the first failure, report done and remaining counts, exit 1, keep the journal for undo.
Quality bar:
- Dry run and apply share the same plan code.
- A second apply changes nothing.
- Undo restores names and contents exactly.
Pitfalls:
- Case only renames (a.txt to A.txt) on case insensitive disks; go through a temp name.
- Planning and applying in one loop, so conflicts appear halfway.
Verify:
- [ ] Dry run is default and touches nothing.
- [ ] Conflict check runs before any change.
- [ ] Temp file then rename for writes.
- [ ] Journal written before each step.
Output: bin/batch.mjs, src/plan.mjs, src/apply.mjs and tests for plan conflicts.

examples.input: renomear 2000 fotos por data com previa antes e como desfazer
examples.output: bin/batch.mjs building a plan, conflict check, --dry-run listing, --apply with temp then rename, .batch-undo.jsonl and batch undo
